the role of PLD-derived PA in TPA-induced signal transduction.
the identification of second messenger molecules in the activation of signal transduction pathways.
elucidating the mechanism(s) of PLD activation and the role(s) of PLDs and their products in cell signaling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PLD-derived metabolites are required in the signal transduction pathway for TPA-induced PGHS-2 synthesis.
PLD-derived phospholipids are required for the activation of Raf-1 and the sustained activation of PKC, which are required for the induction of PGH2 synthase-2.
PLD-derived metabolites, PA and DG are involved in TPA-stimulation of PGHS-1/PGHS-2 expression in MDCK cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TPA-stimulate PGE2 synthesis by a PKC-dependent activation of PLD which results in the formation of PA.
PLD activation by TPA is required for the induction of PGH-2, which in turn is required for prolonged prostaglandin biosynthesis.
TPA stimulates PLD activity in MDCK cells, and that the PLD-derived product(s) are required to induce the expression of the PGHS-2 enzyme, which in turn mediates the sustained production of PGE2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PA is an intracellular messenger that is involved in a variety of signal transduction pathways.
PA and DG are not the only PLD products.
the activation of phospholipases C (PLC) and PLD are not necessarily mutually exclusive.
